hypothesis: Observed-only attribution: production exit-lifecycle high-pressure rows that are still above cost at the advisory time should show worse next-5-trading-day outcomes than above-cost no-advisory rows, proving the forward-loss lead is not only a current-loss label.
new_evidence_axis: PIT unrealized_pnl_pct at the advisory time splits above-cost winner giveback from below-cost current-loss labeling; this is not a retry of raw exit severity, LLM state confluence, target trim, target-width, or fixed-entry oracle regret buckets.

parameters.cost_state_definition: above_cost when PIT unrealized_pnl_pct >= 0 at the advisory as_of date; below_cost otherwise.
parameters.outcome_definition: Gross diagnostic return from next trading session open after as_of_date to the close five trading days later; no order is scheduled and no execution cost is applied.

post_run_reflection.forbidden_near_neighbor_retry: Do not retry by converting above-cost high-urgency, below-cost hard-stop, target, trailing-stop, time-stop, MFE/giveback, or target-width labels into executable rules on the same forward rows. A valid retry needs materially more closed rows, slot-reuse/winner-collateral accounting, and a predeclared shared default-off advisory helper.
post_run_reflection.new_evidence_required: More closed production exit-lifecycle rows with next-open settlement, explicit slot-reuse/winner-collateral accounting, and a shared default-off advisory lifecycle helper before any Gate 1-4 exit-policy promotion.
post_run_reflection.why_result_happened: Above-cost advisory rows did show negative forward separation, but the target loss bucket was too concentrated in one ticker. That makes the result a fragile clue, not an exit or risk rule.
